content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have successfully established communication between [product_name] and [product_name] on my PC, as shown in the attached files. I'm wondering if it is possible to replace [product_name] with [product_name] for this setup. My goal is to build an application that supports communication with 50 instances of [product_name], each having a separate connection to the PC (there will not be any communication between the [product_name] modules themselves—just 50 direct connections to the PC). Thanks in advance!

Hi, Connecting 50 [product_name] modules to [product_name] should also function as expected. Keep in mind that in this arrangement, the first of the 8 available channels will be shared by 42 [product_name] units. Regarding [product_name], I don't have experience.

Hello, It is likely possible to use [product_name] OPC as well. Just check which versions of [product_name] are compatible with which versions of [product_name]—more details can be found in [document]. Instead of [product_name], try assigning another supported product (as in "How can you set up a connection between a [product_name] and an operator panel?"). Also, you'll need an extra license ([product_name]) to support over 8 connections. It's worth trying, though sometimes [product_name] is the cheaper solution. Best regards, [user_name]

Hello everyone, Thanks for your feedback. [user_name], could you please provide some additional details about your idea? I'm not sure how to connect 42 [product_name] modules on the first channel of [product_name].
Hi, There’s no trick to it; just add your 42 IP addresses to [product_name]. The first channel will be utilized automatically, so no special action is needed.
Hello! Can someone explain why changing the TSAP value of the server causes data exchange issues? Everything works only if TSAP is set to 25.00. What's the reason for this?

Hi, I connected a [product_name] module to a PC (Windows XP) via [product_name]. I discovered that [product_name] is unable to work with the TSAP automatically used for the first channel in [product_name]. When you configure a server connection in [product_name], that channel gets TSAP 20.00, but [product_name] does not support it. To resolve this, set up a second server connection which will use TSAP 21.00, and then [product_name] works properly. In [product_name], you should add all modules as a generic station and specify the correct TSAP values (remote TSAP set to 21.00; local TSAP can be the same, but it's adjustable). Hope this helps.

[user_name], thank you for your help! I was confused by using TSAP 25.00 for the server, and all my attempts to make a program with the default TSAP 20.00 failed. Now I understand what was causing the issue! Changing the local TSAP works fine—I’ve verified it. Previously, I tested [product_name] + [product_name] with a SCADA system and it operated perfectly in both directions. For me, this is a significant enhancement in using [product_name] as part of an automation system including an operator’s workstation based on PC. There was an issue with [product_name] not running on Windows 7, but using Oracle VirtualBox solved it easily. Thanks again!

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for methods to connect multiple [product_name] modules to PC applications by using different communication products. While [product_name] software is working, some users consider switching to [product_name] for better scalability and compatibility with their application. There is some confusion about channel management and limitations of TSAP configuration. Compatibility issues with updated Windows environments were mentioned, along with practical workarounds.
